description: Essential works of world literature and their literary significance

iliad_odyssey.author: Homer (attributed)
iliad_odyssey.significance: Foundation of Western literary tradition; themes of heroism, fate, homecoming

epic_of_gilgamesh.significance: Oldest known written epic; themes of friendship, mortality, quests

aeneid.author: Virgil
aeneid.significance: Roman national epic; foundation of Rome myth; influenced Dante

divine_comedy.author: Dante Alighieri
divine_comedy.summary: Journey through Hell (Inferno), Purgatory, and Paradise; allegory of souls path to God

canterbury_tales.author: Geoffrey Chaucer
canterbury_tales.significance: Diverse portraits of English medieval society; pilgrimage framing device

don_quixote.author: Miguel de Cervantes
don_quixote.significance: First modern novel; themes of reality vs. illusion, idealism

pride_and_prejudice.author: Jane Austen
themes: marriage and class in Regency England

war_and_peace.author: Leo Tolstoy
war_and_peace.significance: Epic spanning Napoleonic Wars; explores free will vs. historical determinism

one_hundred_years_of_solitude.author: Gabriel García Márquez
one_hundred_years_of_solitude.significance: Defining work of magical realism; saga of Buendía family in Macondo

in_search_of_lost_time.author: Marcel Proust
in_search_of_lost_time.significance: 7-volume masterpiece on memory, time, and art; madeleine scene iconic

ulysses.author: James Joyce
ulysses.significance: Modernist epic; single day in Dublin; stream of consciousness technique

literary_devices.irony: Saying the opposite of what is meant, or outcome opposite of expectations
literary_devices.allusion: Indirect reference to another work or event
literary_devices.motif: Recurring element that has symbolic significance
